To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

feeding high proportions (30 to 45%) of barley grain in the diets of dairy cows was associated with lower dry matter intake and milk production and increased endotoxin content in the rumen, and that this was associated with an inflammatory response.

feeding high proportions of barley to dairy cows is associated with reduced feed intake and ruminal pH, increased endotoxicity in the rumen, and increased concentrations of plasma proteins associated with inflammation.

feeding high proportions of barley in the diet of lactating dairy cows was associated with reduced feed intake and milk production and increased ruminal endotoxin and plasma concentrations of serum amyloids A and C reactive protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of feeding high proportions of grain on the acute phase response in dairy cows and the possible consequences on health.
the effect of high grain feeding on the acute phase response of dairy cows.
the effects of barley grain on the inflammatory response in dairy cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the feeding of high proportions of barley in the diet of dairy cows was associated with lower dry matter intake, lower ruminal pH, and increased ruminal endotoxin and an inflammatory response.
feeding high proportions of barley in the diet of lactating dairy cows may stimulate the inflammatory response.
feeding high proportions of barley grains to dairy cows may be detrimental for their health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high-grain feeding in dairy cows stimulates an inflammatory response, and the magnitude of response increases with increasing grain proportions.
barley grain is not an appropriate feedstuff for dairy cows, and the proportion of barley grain should be limited to less than 15% of the diet.
feeding high proportions of barley to lactating dairy cows is not a good practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feeding high proportions of barley to dairy cows can lead to an inflammatory response, which could be detrimental to cow health.
feeding high proportions of barley grains to dairy cows may increase risk of subacute ruminal acidosis, and that this may be associated with an inflammatory response.
barley grain should be included in diets of lactating cows at low to moderate proportions (15 to 30% DM basis).
